text:
elaine: Quick sync — proposing a staged operator upgrade playbook for private deploys (VPC/on‑prem) that targets zero-drift during rolling upgrades. High-level phases: canary per-tenant -> validation -> gradual ramp -> cutover -> cleanup. aim is no config drift and clear rollback markers.
sanjay: love the structure. can we make the canary tenant opt-in (label-based) so field can trigger without extra infra? :+1:
marco: two non-negotiables: operator image immutability (digest pin) and migration idempotency checks. otherwise we get flaky state transitions.
tess: agree. also need a preflight that verifies KMS/HSM access + egress rules for onprem customers (we keep hitting edge cases where telemetry egress is blocked).
elaine: good call. preflight checklist idea: kernel version, iptables rules, outbound endpoints allowed, kms reachable, disk pressure low, available pod CIDR. lightweight to run locally.
rachel: for airgapped installs, preflight should include artifact bundle hash verification and operatorctl version compatibility matrix. we should publish a minimal cli to run these checks.
marco: for rollback semantics we should write a short marker file approach: operator writes /var/lib/redwood/upgrade-marker with status {pending, success, failed, rolled_back}. the controller watches and avoids double-apply.
sanjay: marker file is fine but we also want a second-level marker in the control-plane audit log so infra teams can correlate. ops-bot: recorded event if marker flips to failed -> notify #eng-oncall.
ops-bot: NOTE: we can integrate with existing rollout-webhook to emit an event on each phase transition.
tess: what about DB migrations? need an explicit no-blocking-migrations rule: zero-downtime safe migrations only, and migrations must be reversible within upgrade window.
elaine: proposal: any schema changes must be behind feature flags and rolled out in two steps (write+backfill then read-remove). add an emergency rollback runbook in the playbook.
marco: how long per-tenant ramp? suggest canary 1h monitoring, then 5% for 6h, 25% for 12h, then 100% over 48h. these numbers flexible but SLOs should gate progress.
sanjay: +automated health gates: cpu, p95 latency, error-rate, KV-cache-miss spike. if any gate trips, auto pause and rollback to previous operator digest.
rachel: ops note: customers sometimes pin operator version in their packaging. we need a clear migration path: operator shim that supports both old/new CRD versions during handoff.
tess: packaging detail: create two installer presets — "compat" and "minimal". compat includes shim and conversion hooks, minimal is for greenfield.
elaine: upgrade window expectations: default policy = automated-staged with 7-day rollback window for critical customers; field can opt for manual. we should capture these as launch criteria.
marco: logging + observability: every upgrade must stream per-tenant trace id and a short diff of CRD manifests applied. keep diffs < 1MB.
sanjay: build a lightweight dry-run mode for the operator that outputs planned diffs (no apply) and verifies idempotency. helpful for field ops.
elaine: draft playbook outline I want to ship: 1) preflight CLI, 2) canary config + label, 3) operator digest pinning + shim, 4) health gates + auto-pause, 5) marker + audit events, 6) rollback steps + telemetry, 7) airgap artifact bundle guide.
rachel: can you add permissions checklist for customers (RBAC rules) — we saw installs fail with insufficient CRD-level permissions.
elaine: will add. follow-ups: can someone prototype the dry-run output format and a minimal preflight CLI by next Wed?
sanjay: i'll take dry-run format, small jsonlines output with per-resource actions.
marco: i'll sketch preflight CLI and artifact verification steps.
tess: i'll compile selector/label guidance for canary tenants + installer presets.
elaine: thanks team. i'll assemble playbook doc and share a draft before EOD Friday. :spiral_note_pad:
ops-bot: ACTION: created RFC draft ticket RF-4821 with initial outline and assigned to elaine, sanjay, marco, tess.
elaine: pinging product-ops for launch criteria review once draft is up.
marco: one last thing — add a short troubleshooting matrix for common network failure modes (DNS blocked, egress firewall, MTU issues). saves time during field rollouts.
elaine: added to todo. closing thread for now, but please react with :eyes: when you review the draft.
